correctness.rationale: The proof reuses the exact Section 6 inequalities from arXiv:2609.38032v1. For arbitrary a>1, the source radius-selection proof gives r integral H(at)/(r+t)^2 <= I_{alpha,a} H(r). If c exceeds the limsup N1/T, the translated source inequalities give N_y(t)<=c H_y(at)+C once t is large, with the bounded interval absorbed into C. For alpha>rho, H_y=o(r^alpha). If c I_{alpha,a}<1, Corollary 6.3 gives logarithmic growth of H_y along unbounded radii, and Cauchy estimates force all coordinates to be polynomials, contradicting transcendence. Continuity as alpha down to rho and a down to one yields the claimed constant. The half-order evaluation and rho-to-one asymptotic follow from the defining integral.

value.rationale: The fresh source makes the order-zero Wronskian-density inequality a separate sharp theorem and leaves positive subunit orders with only the qualitative implication N1=o(T) => rational. The accepted result fills that natural quantitative gap with a dimension-independent explicit function of rho, gives a concrete half-order constant 4/(4+pi), and identifies the linear scale as rho approaches one. It measures forced inflection mass for every transcendental curve in the entire subunit-order regime rather than supplying a routine numerical special case.
